65fc1b6bb8.why: Load the next input directly into xmm1 and reload it later into the required final xmm0. This eliminates one copy while preserving xmm7, both stores, and the comparison flags.

3228e78398.why: The half-width count requires a copy and shift, while the counter zeroing, address calculation, and live constant load are independent required results.

b687c7729f.why: SSE2 requires the two inputs, word sum, preserved copy for both interleaves, two stores, and live loop update.

f717f452d3.why: The arbitrary xmm3 addends, arithmetic shifts, and separate low/high interleaves leave no redundant operation in this SSE2 sequence.

0b87c8b55c.why: All four instructions write required registers, and the subtraction also produces the required flags.

cc4a0390d8.why: The three address updates, counter subtraction, and register copy all produce independently required final values.

1bdb122d3d.why: The byte expansion and weighted arithmetic are needed under SSE2, including the contributions from arbitrary xmm7 values before shifting and saturation.

dc89b8bcbf.why: Both unpacked halves are needed for each product, and the potentially unaligned destination loads cannot safely fold into legacy PADDW memory operands.

7788939c88.why: Both unpacked halves and all scalar updates are live, while folding the destination loads into legacy PADDW would impose an additional alignment requirement.

a1230b6476.why: The unpacked multiplication and unaligned destination load are necessary, and every pointer and counter update is live.

7d7666124e.why: The absolute value, multiply, bias, logical shift, and zero-aware sign restoration each affect the result, while the loaded xmm0 and scalar updates must remain live.
